To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the casein molecule has an extended, rod-like structure, with a diameter of about 3 nm and a length of about 6 nm.

the casein micellar structure is maintained by a network of hydrophobic interactions and that the casein submicelle is stabilized by hydrophobic interactions, electrostatic repulsion, and hydrogen bonding.

(a) the casein micelles are not a simple aggregation of submicelles, (b) the submicelle is a dynamic structure with a lifetime of the order of 100 μsec, and (c) there is a strong interaction between the submicelles and the water.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure, stability, and dynamics of the bovine αs1-casein molecule in solution, in the presence and absence of calcium.
the structure of the submicelles, which are formed by the removal of calcium from the micelles.
the study of water interactions with the protein molecules of bovine casein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the caseins are a heterogeneous mixture of proteins that have a high degree of hydrophobicity, are highly acidic (pI < 5), are rich in hydrophobic amino acid residues, and contain large amounts of phosphate (Eigel et aI., 1984).
casein is a hydrophobic protein with a high content of phosphoserine.
the casein micelles are a colloidal complex of the four caseins, calcium, inorganic phosphate, and magnesium (Fox, 1982; Farrell, 1988).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
water molecules are bound to casein molecules in the casein micelles and that the bound water is not exchangeable with the free water.
the 2H N.M.R. results are consistent with the view of the submicelle as a highly dynamic structure in solution, in which there is a rapid exchange between water and protein-bound water molecules.
the water dynamics in the protein interior is not very different from that in bulk water, but that the water dynamics is affected by the protein surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the casein micellar structure is very complex and that it is difficult to study the structure of the micelle in a meaningful way.
the caseins are very hydrophobic proteins.
the casein micelles are very complex structures and that the sub-micelle model is not sufficient for understanding their structure and function.
